true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Website-name inclusion predicate has the wrong serializer method name

The serializer convention used throughout this class is `include_<attribute>?` (for example `include_card_image_badge_id?`). This method is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, so ActiveModel serialization will not use it as the inclusion predicate. Consequently `website_name` is treated as an unconditional attribute and can be emitted as null for present-but-unparseable website values; more importantly, the intended guard is not actually enforcing any visibility policy. Rename it to `include_website_name?` and make that predicate honor the website visibility restriction.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same core bug: include_website_name lacks the required trailing ? so ActiveModel serializers won't treat it as the conditional inclusion predicate. The candidate omits the secondary string-concatenation concern but points to the same primary issue.

false_positives.candidate:
`website_name` bypasses TL0 profile-field restrictions

`website_name` is serialized independently of `website`, but it is not included in `untrusted_attributes`. For anonymous views of a TL0 user, `include_website?` suppresses the actual website while this new attribute still exposes its hostname and, for matching instance domains, its full path. This defeats the existing privacy restriction for the website profile field. Apply the same restriction to `website_name` (or make its inclusion depend on `include_website?`) and add coverage for an anonymous TL0 serialization.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Imported feed/article HTML is persisted without sanitization

`import` creates posts with `cook_method: raw_html`, and `Post#cook` returns this content verbatim. `contents` comes directly from RSS/Atom feeds or a remotely fetched page and is neither sanitized nor escaped before becoming `post.cooked`; it also interpolates the unescaped source URL into an HTML attribute on line 13. A malicious article/feed item can therefore store script/event-handler HTML that executes for users viewing the imported topic (and in the embed view, which renders `raw post.cooked`). Sanitize imported HTML and URLs with the normal allowlist before storing/rendering it rather than bypassing the cooking pipeline.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same XSS vulnerability: imported feed/article HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized, and the source URL is interpolated unescaped into an HTML attribute. It omits the separate nil-contents NoMethodError, but the core security issue matches.

false_positives.candidate:
Remote import follows redirects without enforcing the allowed host

The retriever validates only the host of the initial `embed_url`, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects and this method does not validate each redirect target or block private/reserved addresses. An unauthenticated caller can request an allowed-host URL that redirects to an internal service (for example via an open redirect on the configured site), causing the Discourse server to fetch internal endpoints. Enforce the host/address policy on every redirect hop (and reject private/link-local targets), or use an HTTP client configured not to follow redirects.

Relative links without a leading slash are not converted to source URLs

Despite the method's contract to convert relative URLs, it only rewrites `href` and `src` values beginning with `/`. Common document-relative URLs such as `images/photo.jpg`, `../article`, or `?page=2` remain unchanged. Once the content is displayed on Discourse, browsers resolve those URLs relative to the forum/embed URL rather than the original article, producing broken or incorrectly directed links and images. Resolve all non-absolute URLs against the full source URL (for example with `URI.join`).

The success-path spec expects a retriever call that the controller no longer makes

This example sets an expectation that `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` is invoked, but `EmbedController#best` now calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` instead. The expectation is unsatisfied whenever this example runs, so the newly added controller spec fails rather than testing the asynchronous behavior. Update it to assert the queued job and its arguments.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The existing four-dimension `downsize` API has been removed by Ruby method redefinition

Ruby does not overload methods. The new definition at line 149 replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition, so callers using the previously supported width/height form now receive `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments`. The preceding definition is therefore dead code. Keep a single implementation that accepts both forms (or update all existing callers and intentionally change the contract).
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the duplicate downsize definitions and Ruby redefinition overriding the original width/height API, breaking existing callers.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side upload validation no longer honors configured attachment and image limits

This replaces `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` with a hard-coded 10 MB limit for every upload type. Sites with a smaller attachment limit will now let users select files that the server subsequently rejects, and sites configured to allow files larger than 10 MB will have those uploads blocked in the browser. Automatic image reduction does not justify applying a fixed image-sized limit to non-image attachments; retain the configured limit for attachments and make any larger-image allowance explicit and consistent with server behavior.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: replacing per-type configured upload limits (max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb) with a hardcoded 10 MB client-side cap, causing client/server limit divergence. The candidate captures the same root cause and consequences, even without explicitly naming the 413 handler.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
A GET request changes a user's notification state

The `unsubscribe` action is exposed as a GET route and explicitly skips the XHR/CSRF protection, but it writes `TopicUser.notification_level`. Any third-party page can cause a logged-in user's browser to request a known `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` URL (for example via an image), muting or changing that user's topic notifications without consent. Link scanners and prefetchers can also trigger the mutation. Make the state change a CSRF-protected non-GET request, or use a purpose-bound signed unsubscribe token that is safe to consume from an email link.

The unsubscribe link does not reliably unsubscribe watched/tracked users

For notification levels above `regular`, following the email's “stop receiving notifications” link changes the level only to `regular`, not `muted`. Regular users can still receive topic notifications such as replies or mentions, so the link's stated result is not achieved. It also makes the outcome dependent on the current level: a second invocation changes regular to muted, while an initial invocation for a watcher does not. Set the intended unsubscribed state directly (normally `muted`) so the operation is idempotent.

Directly saving TopicUser bypasses notification-change bookkeeping

This action mutates and saves the TopicUser row directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`, which is the established path for notification-level changes. As a result it does not set `notifications_changed_at`, does not mark `notifications_reason_id` as `user_changed`, and does not publish the MessageBus notification-level update. In particular, a row whose reason remains nil may subsequently be auto-promoted back to tracking by `update_last_read`, undoing the unsubscribe; active clients can also continue to display stale notification state. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` rather than assigning and saving the record.

false_negatives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook setup script uses a macOS-only sed invocation

`sed -i '' -E` is BSD/macOS syntax. On Linux, where GNU sed treats the empty string differently, this command fails after Tunnelmole has been started, so `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is not updated and local webhook testing cannot work as advertised. Use a portable file-replacement approach or branch on the installed sed implementation.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: the script uses macOS/BSD-specific `sed -i ''` syntax that fails under GNU sed on Linux, preventing the webhook URL from being updated. The wording and added consequence do not change the underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Deleting cache does not refresh the connected-calendars cache status

The delete mutation only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback. This component is also rendered with no guarantee that callback invalidates/refetches `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (and it may be absent), unlike the disconnect mutation which explicitly invalidates its dependent queries. Consequently, after a successful deletion the UI continues to receive/render the old `cacheUpdatedAt`, still reporting cached data and offering the delete action until an unrelated refresh or reload. Invalidate or update the connectedCalendars query when the delete mutation settles successfully.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours validation ignores the event duration

Both `start` and `end` are calculated from `slotStartTime`, so the new fixed-host working-hours validation only verifies that the slot start is before the end of availability. For example, a 60-minute event starting at 16:30 is accepted for a host whose hours end at 17:00. This can expose round-robin slots that the fixed host cannot actually attend; `end` needs to include `eventLength`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the end time is incorrectly derived from slotStartTime rather than the actual slot end/event duration, so working-hours validation can accept events that extend past availability.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Zero-length date overrides are never recognized as equal

`dayjs(...) === dayjs(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false even when `start` and `end` represent the same instant. A zero-length override, which represents an unavailable date/time, therefore falls through to the range checks; notably the slot beginning exactly at the override instant is treated as available. This allows bookings during an explicitly blocked override. Compare the instants with `isSame` (or timestamps) instead.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: dayjs object comparison with === checks references and is always false, so equal start/end instants (zero-length overrides) are missed. Both recommend comparing instants with isSame (or timestamps).

false_positives.candidate:
Fixed hosts with multiple working-hour ranges are checked as an intersection

The working-hours check returns unavailable as soon as the slot is outside any matching range because it uses `find` with an out-of-range predicate. For a common split schedule such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a 10:00 slot is outside the second range and a 14:00 slot is outside the first, so every slot is rejected for the fixed host. The check must instead accept a slot if it fits at least one applicable working-hour range.

Multiple date-override ranges on one day are treated as mutually exclusive

The callback passed to `dateOverrides.find` returns true when a slot is outside any one override range. Consequently, if a host has two availability override windows on the same date, a slot inside the first window is outside the second and is rejected. Date override ranges should be combined as a union: the slot should be accepted when it fits at least one override range, and rejected only when it fits none.

No regression test covers the fixed-host round-robin behavior claimed by this PR

The added test only exercises a single-host event's override under two nearby time zones. It does not create a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host and a loose host, nor verify that an override or normal fixed-host availability removes otherwise available loose-host slots. The new `checkIfIsAvailable` path is only used for that host filtering and currently has range-handling defects that this missing scenario would have caught.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry count updates can lose increments under overlapping cron runs

The handler reads `reminder.retryCount` and later writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`. Two concurrent cron invocations can both select the same unscheduled reminder, both fail to schedule it, and both write the same value (for example, 1). This loses one failure, prevents the retry limit from being reached reliably, and both invocations can issue duplicate provider scheduling calls. Use an atomic database increment and claim/conditionally update the reminder before scheduling to ensure only one worker processes a reminder.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same race: reading reminder.retryCount and writing retryCount + 1 can lose increments under concurrent cron runs. The candidate's atomic increment recommendation matches the golden fix, with extra detail about claiming the reminder.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry-limit deletion is not restricted to SMS reminders

The second branch of this `OR` filters only on `retryCount`, so any `WorkflowReminder` method (including EMAIL or WHATSAPP) with a count above one will be deleted by the SMS scheduling cron. The retry cleanup condition should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or the outer query should constrain the method) so this endpoint cannot remove reminders owned by other delivery mechanisms.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the retryCount branch of the deletion OR lacks a WorkflowMethods.SMS constraint, so the SMS scheduling cleanup can delete EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders with retryCount > 1.

false_positives.candidate:
The condition permits a third scheduling attempt after two failures

A reminder starts at `retryCount = 0`; its first and second failed attempts set the count to 1 and 2. On the next cron run `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` is evaluated only before scheduling, so the row is deleted then, but it will already have been eligible for the second failure? More specifically, after the first failure it is retried; after the second failure it becomes 2 and is removed on the following run. This produces two attempts, but the cleanup timing leaves a persisted failed reminder. If the intended contract is to delete immediately after the second failed scheduling attempt, the failure update should delete at the limit or use a transaction/conditional operation. Otherwise the stated behavior is delayed until the next cron execution and failed rows remain available to other workers.

Reminders with no recipient or generated message still retry forever

Retry count is incremented only when `scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value or throws. If `sendTo` is empty (for example, an attendee has no SMS number) or template generation leaves `message` empty, this condition is skipped without marking the reminder scheduled, failed, or exhausted. The reminder therefore remains in every cron query until its scheduled date, retaining the infinite retry behavior this change is intended to stop. Treat an unsendable reminder as a failed attempt or explicitly delete/cancel it.

The public findMany API was removed without a replacement query API

This change deletes `InsightsBookingService.findMany`, which previously executed the authorized `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` query and accepted normal Prisma findMany arguments. The only replacement is `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a SQL fragment and requires every caller to reimplement query execution, selection, pagination, ordering, and safe composition. Existing consumers invoking `service.findMany(...)` will fail to compile (or fail at runtime for untyped consumers), and no caller migrations are included in this PR. Preserve a compatible execution method or update all consumers as part of the same change.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google refresh persists the Zod parse-result wrapper as the credential key

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParse result object (`{ success, data }`), unlike the former `googleCredentialSchema.parse` call which returned the credential payload itself. This code stores that wrapper in `Credential.key` at line 100. On the next request `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` receives `{success,data}` rather than Google token fields and rejects the credential, so a successfully refreshed Google integration becomes unusable.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same root issue: the code stores the Zod safeParse wrapper returned by the JSON response instead of extracting the actual credential/token data. It correctly explains that the response shape must be handled and the relevant credential fields extracted before persisting.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
HubSpot sync treats a Fetch Response as a HubSpot token object

When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch`, i.e. a `Response`, but this caller casts it directly to `HubspotToken` and reads `expiresIn`, `accessToken`, and serializes it into the credential. Unlike the normal HubSpot SDK path, it never calls `response.json()`. Consequently synced HubSpot refreshes produce undefined/invalid token fields and can fail to save a valid credential or authenticate subsequent API calls.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same credential-sync return-type mismatch: refresh returns a fetch Response, but the HubSpot caller treats it as a HubspotToken without parsing JSON, producing invalid token data. This is the HubSpot-specific instance of the broader issue described in the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Zoho CRM sync path never parses the remote Fetch response

Without syncing this code receives an Axios response and accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data`. With syncing enabled `refreshOAuthTokens` instead returns a native `Response`, and no `.json()` call is made before accessing `.data`. The refreshed credential therefore has no token payload and Zoho CRM calendar operations fail whenever the sync endpoint is used.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: the sync path returns a native fetch Response, but the code still treats it like an Axios response and reads .data without parsing JSON, so the token payload is missing and Zoho CRM operations fail.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Zoho Bigin sync uses a Fetch Response as though it were an Axios response

The normal refresh callback returns an Axios response with a `.data` payload, but the sync branch in `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch` `Response`. The subsequent code reads and mutates `tokenInfo.data` without parsing the response body, so with syncing enabled it cannot obtain an access token and attempts to persist/use invalid values. In addition, the third argument is `credentialId`, which is sent as `calcomUserId`; credential IDs are not user IDs, so the remote app is asked for the wrong user's token.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the same bug: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId as the third argument, which is sent as calcomUserId, so the remote app looks up the wrong user. The extra Fetch-vs-Axios point does not negate the match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Salesforce connection is initialized with the expired pre-refresh token

After obtaining and saving `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`, the connection is still constructed with `credentialKey.access_token`, which is the token that prompted the refresh. The current request therefore authenticates to Salesforce with the expired token and fails; only a later service construction that rereads the database could use the saved token.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: after refreshing the Salesforce token, the jsforce connection is still initialized with the stale pre-refresh credentialKey.access_token, causing the current request to authenticate with the expired token. The candidate captures this core issue even though it does not explicitly mention instance_url.

false_positives.candidate:
Salesforce service references Prisma without importing it

The newly added credential update calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this module has no `prisma` import. This fails TypeScript compilation (`Cannot find name 'prisma'`) and, if type checking is bypassed, throws a `ReferenceError` whenever the Salesforce service initializes.

Salesforce refresh bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint

This new refresh implementation always posts the stored refresh token and app secret directly to Salesforce rather than using `refreshOAuthTokens`. Thus Salesforce is included in the changed integrations but continues to make Cal.com the refresh-token holder/source of truth, contrary to the credential-sync feature; deployments enabling sync cannot refresh Salesforce credentials through their external app store.

Credential-sync token requests contain no authentication

The outbound request identifies a user solely by the predictable `calcomUserId` and app slug and sends neither the configured webhook secret nor any signature/authorization header. A self-hosted app-store endpoint has no information with which to distinguish a Cal.com refresh request from an arbitrary caller requesting another user's integration token. The documented secret is only checked on the reverse webhook and does not protect this endpoint.

Zoom requests a different app slug than the credential's configured app ID

The Zoom callback creates credentials with `appId: "zoom"`, but the refresh-sync request sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"`. The sync API is explicitly keyed by app slug, so a source application that maps credentials by the configured app ID will not find Zoom credentials and cannot return a refreshed token.

Webhook credential upsert is race-prone and can create duplicate credentials

The handler implements an upsert as a separate `findFirst` followed by `create`, with no transaction or database uniqueness constraint. Concurrent sync webhooks for the same user and app can both observe no credential and both create one. Multiple credentials for an integration cause nondeterministic `findFirst` selection and leave stale third-party tokens in the database.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reminder cancellation writes are not awaited before completing booking cancellation

`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async, but the nested `forEach` discards their promises. Consequently the booking cancellation request can complete while the email reminder's `cancelled` update or SMS cancellation/delete is still pending. In a serverless/request-scoped runtime those operations can be interrupted after the response, and the cron can observe the reminder before it is marked, resulting in a reminder being sent for a cancelled booking. Collect and await these operations (and apply the same treatment in the other modified cancellation paths).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are not awaited inside forEach loops during cancellation paths, so reminder cancellation may not complete reliably.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Standard reschedules still immediately consume SendGrid cancellation slots

The reschedule flow passes `true` for `immediateDelete`, causing `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to call SendGrid immediately rather than mark the reminder as cancelled for the cron-based cleanup. This preserves the old behavior that accumulates SendGrid scheduled-send cancellations and hits the provider's 100 pending-cancellation limit during reschedules. Errors are swallowed by the helper and no `cancelled` flag is set as a fallback, so reminders whose immediate cancellation is rejected will still be sent.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments target the immediateDelete=true path in deleteScheduledEmailReminder: it performs immediate SendGrid cancellation without updating/deleting the WorkflowReminder record (no cancelled flag), leaving inconsistent/orphaned state. The candidate adds the rate-limit consequence, but the underlying bug is the same.

false_positives.candidate:
Past-due cleanup drops cancelled reminders before they are cancelled at SendGrid

The handler deletes every email reminder whose scheduledDate is in the past before querying and cancelling `cancelled` reminders. If a booking is cancelled shortly before its reminder and the next 15-minute cron invocation occurs after the reminder's send time, this deletion removes the only cancellation record and no SendGrid cancellation request is made. The already scheduled SendGrid email can therefore still be delivered, which is precisely the case this change is intended to prevent. Cancelled reminders must be handled before cleanup, and cancellation should not depend on a cron execution occurring before `sendAt`.

The cron's SendGrid client is never authenticated

This module configures only `sgMail` with `sgMail.setApiKey`; it never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` for the separately imported `@sendgrid/client` instance. The new cancellation request at this line uses that client directly, so it will be sent without SendGrid authorization and fail. The catch only logs the failure, leaving the reminder in the database and allowing the email to be sent.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guest and blacklist comparisons are case-sensitive

Email addresses are compared directly against stored attendees and the lowercased blacklist, but input guest addresses are never normalized. A request using a different case can bypass `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` and can add a second logical copy of an existing attendee (or trigger a database uniqueness failure, depending on collation/constraints). Normalize and compare email addresses case-insensitively before filtering, persistence, and deciding which recipients are new.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team administrators are rejected by an ANDed role check

The authorization check requires the caller to satisfy both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`. Team membership roles are distinct, so an administrator who is not the booking's organizer fails this condition and receives FORBIDDEN, despite the product UI treating team admins or owners as eligible (`isUserTeamAdminOrOwner`). Use an OR check so either role can manage a team booking.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same incorrect AND role check that should be OR so either team admin or owner is authorized.

false_positives.candidate:
The guest list has no server-side size limit

Any authenticated attendee is authorized to call this endpoint, and `guests` is an unbounded array. A caller can submit thousands of arbitrary valid addresses in one request, creating corresponding attendee records, calendar invitations, and emails; repeated calls also notify every existing attendee. This makes the endpoint an email-spam and resource-exhaustion primitive. Enforce a reasonable maximum number of guests server-side (and ideally a per-booking/event-type guest policy).

Attendees are persisted before calendar synchronization succeeds

The handler writes the new attendees to the booking before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`. If the calendar update fails (for example, because an attendee/admin actor lacks the organizer's calendar credentials), the mutation rejects but the database still shows the guests as added, while the external calendar and notification flow were not updated. This leaves booking state inconsistent and retries can behave differently. The operation needs compensation/outbox handling or a deliberate failure strategy that does not leave the completed database mutation presented as a failed add.

The endpoint permits adding guests to cancelled or rejected bookings

Authorization is the only booking-state validation; a direct API caller who was an attendee, organizer, or team manager can add guests to a cancelled or rejected booking. The handler then creates attendee records and sends confirmed calendar/email updates for an event that will not occur. Restrict this mutation to the supported active booking statuses (and any applicable time/recurrence rules) on the server rather than relying on the dashboard action visibility.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup codes are consumed with a non-atomic read-modify-write

The code list is read from the user record, checked in memory, and then written back after replacing the matched entry with `null`. Two concurrent login requests using the same code can both read the old encrypted list before either update occurs, both pass `indexOf`, and both create sessions; the last write merely overwrites the same resulting list. This violates the advertised one-time-use property. Consume the code atomically, for example by using a transaction/row lock or a conditional update that verifies the stored value has not changed and rejects the request when no row was updated.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same race condition: concurrent logins can read the same backup-code list before either write, allowing one code to be accepted twice. The candidate adds a remediation suggestion but identifies the same underlying bug.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup-code requests can bypass the password check by including a dummy TOTP value

The password verification earlier in `authorize` runs only when `credentials.totpCode` is empty, while this new branch accepts a backup code whenever `credentials.backupCode` is set and does not validate the TOTP value. A caller can submit a valid backup code plus any non-empty `totpCode` value and an arbitrary or absent password; this skips password verification and the backup-code branch succeeds. The UI retains the password during the normal flow, but the credentials callback is directly callable. Require password verification independently of whether a TOTP field is present (or otherwise bind completion of the password step to the second-factor request) before accepting a backup code.

The new backup-code authentication and consumption behavior is not tested

The added test coverage only verifies that the setup screen has downloadable/copyable controls; it does not submit a backup code through login or the disable-2FA flow, verify that a valid code succeeds, verify invalid-code handling, or verify that a used code cannot be reused. The test itself leaves these core feature paths as TODOs, so regressions in the newly added authentication branch and one-time-code behavior will not be caught.

This makes newly created organizations lack a slug in non-team-billing deployments and assigns an active slug in the mode that previously retained it only as `metadata.requestedSlug`, changing organization routing/verification behavior unrelated to destination calendars.

false_positives.candidate:
Non-Google collective host events are still created against the first host calendar

The loop creates one event per destination and supplies `destination.externalId` only to the CalendarManager result metadata. CalendarManager passes only `credential.id` to the provider, while the Office365, Lark, and CalDAV `createEvent` implementations ignore that argument and select `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. Consequently, when a collective event has multiple destination calendars, creation using a later host's credential targets the first host's calendar (or fails due to lacking access), while the stored reference claims the later host calendar. Subsequent updates/deletes will then address the wrong event/calendar.

Recurring cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference for every host

For each calendar reference, the recurring-cancellation branch iterates every calendar credential but selects `updBooking.references.find(...)`, which always returns only the first calendar reference. With multiple host calendar references, it repeatedly tries to delete that first event using unrelated credentials and never processes the remaining references. This leaves recurring events on some host calendars and can issue deletion attempts against the wrong account.

Google Meet description patch no longer uses the primary-calendar fallback

Insertion falls back to `calendarId: "primary"` when no matching destination calendar is found, but the follow-up patch uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which is undefined in that case. Google requires a calendar ID for `events.patch`, so events created in the primary fallback path can fail the asynchronous patch and retain an incomplete description/hangout-link information.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedule cleanup launches unobserved async calendar deletions

Changing this callback to `async` without replacing `forEach` with an awaited `Promise.all` means the new `await getCalendar()` and the subsequent `deleteEvent()` are detached from `Reschedule`. The surrounding `try/catch` does not catch rejections from async `forEach` callbacks, so a failed dynamic import or external calendar deletion is unhandled while the function continues to send the reschedule email and return success. Await the mapped cleanup operations inside the try block.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: the awaited dynamic import/calendar cleanup can fail without being caught by the surrounding error handling. The candidate adds detail about unobserved async forEach callbacks, but the underlying concern matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Recurring calendar deletions are raced against the final cleanup wait

The async `forEach` is not awaited. Since each callback now awaits `getCalendar()` before pushing its deletion promise into `apiDeletes`, execution can reach the later `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` while `apiDeletes` is still empty or incomplete. The cancellation request can therefore finish (and in a serverless worker be terminated) without deleting some recurring events from external calendars, and import/delete failures become unhandled rejections. Build and await a `Promise.all` for these callbacks before relying on `apiDeletes`.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same underlying bug: an async forEach whose callbacks are not awaited, so calendar deletion promises are not reliably collected before cleanup. This causes the same race, incomplete external cleanup, and unhandled rejections described in the golden comment, with an equivalent Promise.all-based fix.

false_positives.candidate:
Request-reschedule returns before asynchronously loaded integrations are deleted

The async callback passed to `forEach` is never awaited. With the new asynchronous `getCalendar`, this mutation marks the booking cancelled and sends the reschedule email before the calendar module has necessarily loaded or its event deletion has run; failures are also unhandled. This can leave the old external calendar/video meeting active even though the booking is cancelled. Collect the callback promises with `map` and await `Promise.all` before completing the mutation.
